summary: Adds an IMAP capability called STATUS=SIZE. With it, a client can ask for the total storage size of a mailbox in a single STATUS command, rather than fetching and adding up the size of every message.

eli5.summary: Instead of weighing every letter in a mailbox one by one, you ask the post office how heavy the whole box is.

questions: how to get imap mailbox size
how to see storage per mailbox in imap
subtitle: Ask an IMAP server for the total size of a mailbox with one STATUS command.

tldr.problem: To learn how big a mailbox is, an IMAP client has to fetch the size of every message and add them up.
tldr.mechanism: The STATUS=SIZE capability adds a SIZE data item to STATUS that returns the total size of all messages in the mailbox in octets, and it works with LIST-STATUS for many mailboxes at once.
tldr.outcome: Clients that do not cache mailbox state, such as most webmail clients, can show per-mailbox storage use with one command.

today: RFC 8438 is a Proposed Standard from August 2018. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: The Problem of Mailbox Size
sections.content:
Without this extension, a client must retrieve every message size with FETCH and the RFC822.SIZE data item to find the total storage size of a mailbox. That is costly for clients that do not cache the state of the message store, such as most webmail clients.

The RFC's example is a user asking for detailed quota usage per mailbox to find which ones need cleaning up. The QUOTA capability (RFC 2087) does not help, because its QUOTAROOT command only reports STORAGE usage for a whole quota root, not each mailbox inside it.
sections.eli5: Adding up every letter's weight takes ages. The post office already knows the total, so you can just ask.

sections.title: The SIZE Data Item
sections.content:
The extension adds one new status data item, SIZE, to the STATUS command and its response. It is the total size of the mailbox in octets. It need not be exact, but it MUST be equal to or greater than the sum of the RFC822.SIZE values of all messages in the mailbox.

When QUOTA is also supported, the value SHOULD equal the storage usage used to enforce the STORAGE limit for that mailbox, so the client can infer quota usage directly.

A server advertises the feature with the capability STATUS=SIZE.
sections.eli5: The server gives one number for the whole box. It can round up a bit, but never says the box is lighter than it really is.

sections.title: Examples and LIST-STATUS
sections.content:
One STATUS command returns the size along with other items. The same information otherwise needs a SELECT followed by FETCH 1:* (RFC822.SIZE) and manual addition, which the RFC calls less efficient.

When the LIST-STATUS capability (RFC 5819) is available, STATUS can be combined with LIST, so the sizes of many mailboxes come back from one LIST command.
sections.eli5: One question gets you the size of one box, and with a bigger question you get the sizes of lots of boxes at once.

sections.title: 63-bit Values and Formal Syntax
sections.content:
A mailbox can easily exceed 4 GB, so clients MUST be able to receive 63-bit SIZE values. The limit is 63 bits rather than 64 to make implementations easier on platforms such as Java.

The ABNF adds STATUS=SIZE as a capability and SIZE as a status attribute, whose value is SIZE SP number64. A number64 is an unsigned 63-bit integer, from 0 up to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807.
sections.eli5: Mailboxes can be huge, so the number field is made big enough for very large totals.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC says there are no known additional security issues beyond those of the base IMAP protocol (RFC 3501) and the LIST-STATUS extension.

IANA added STATUS=SIZE to the IMAP Capabilities registry.
sections.eli5: Telling you a box's size does not open any new doors. A registry keeps a list of the feature names.
